sections.h2: Selling a house in State College
sections.html:
You have three routes: a listing, a private sale, or a straight sale to a buyer who takes the place as it stands. All three end the same way, with a deed recorded in Centre County and the transfer tax paid. What changes from route to route is the prep work and the calendar.

Penn State's University Park campus sits partly inside the borough and partly in neighboring College Township, and it shapes who owns, rents and buys here more than anything else. Population is 40,844, about the same as a decade and a half ago, and the borough covers 4.56 square miles.

Owners live in only 26.1 percent of the homes. The middle owned home is valued at $437,800, gross rent runs $1,273 a month and household income is $45,424. A household averages 2.24 people, and under 6 percent of residents are children.

With so much of the housing rented, the first thing many buyers ask is whether a house carries a rental permit or a student home license. Have those papers in hand before the first showing, and say plainly whether tenants live there now.

sections.h2: Transfer tax in State College Borough
sections.html:
The borough's transfer tax totals 3 percent of the price, against 2 percent in most Centre County municipalities. The county's rate table gives the borough a 1.5 percent local share on top of the state and school district shares.

Realty transfer tax shares, State College Borough and a typical Centre County municipality
Taxing bodyState College BoroughTypical Centre County municipality
State1.00%1.00%
Local (municipality)1.50%0.50%
School district0.50%0.50%
Total3.00%2.00%

No deed gets recorded until the tax is paid. Sales agreements commonly split it down the middle, yet the new owner answers for it if the amount paid is ever questioned, so settle the split before you sign.

Family transfers can be exempt, and so can a deed between ex-spouses. A deed that recites token consideration, such as $1, travels with a state Statement of Value for Department of Revenue review.

sections.h2: Rental permits and student home licenses
sections.html:
These matter in a sale because they decide what a buyer may do with the property after closing. The borough hands rental permit administration to Centre Region Code Administration, which also serves Patton, Ferguson, College, Half Moon and Harris townships and Bellefonte Borough.

  • Rental Housing Permit: required for any unit lived in by someone other than the owner or the owner's immediate family. The unit must meet the International Property Maintenance Code and the Fire Prevention Code. An imminent hazard can bring a vacate order within 10 days, and a suspended permit if the problem is not fixed within 90 days.
  • Student Home License: applies to one-family homes, one-family homes with an accessory apartment, and two-family dwellings occupied by more than one unrelated student. The borough created it with Ordinance 2029 in November 2013. An existing license can pass to a new owner with an approved transfer application and a $25 fee.
  • New student homes: a first license costs $1,000, with a $50 zoning permit for the change of use and a $25 rental permit application fee. In the R-1, R-2 and R-3 zoning districts a new student home must also meet spacing rules from existing ones, which is why a house that already holds a license is worth more to an investor.
  • Short-term rentals: the borough license costs $450 and lasts one year. It requires a rental housing permit, proof the applicant lives there at least eight months a year, off-street parking matching the bedrooms rented, and at least $100,000 of liability insurance.

Student home licenses renew every year. Write to studenthomes@statecollegepa.us to confirm a license is current before you tell a buyer it transfers.

sections.h2: Valley weather and what inspectors look at
sections.html:
The borough sits at about 1,154 feet in a mountain-ringed valley, and rain, snow and flooding are all common on the valley floor. Yearly precipitation is 41.53 inches and snowfall 43.8 inches, with snow usually falling between October and April.

Home inspectors here tend to check sump pumps, foundation moisture, gutters and furnace age. Hand over repair and roof records early, and buyers will have fewer reasons to ask for a credit.

sections.h2: Utilities and schools buyers ask about
sections.html:
New owners set up accounts quickly, so it helps to list the providers in your seller packet. West Penn Power supplies electricity, Columbia Gas of Pennsylvania supplies natural gas, the State College Borough Water Authority provides water, and the University Area Joint Authority handles sewer. Borough public works collects trash and recycling.

The State College Area School District serves the borough. Coral Street, Radio Park and Easterly Parkway elementary schools sit inside it, and Mount Nittany Middle School takes most of the borough's students apart from College Heights. Confirm your own street's assignment with the district before you name a school in your listing.

sections.h2: Which routes sell a State College house fastest?
sections.html:
The quickest routes skip showings and repair haggling. A listing reaches the most people but adds inspection requests, financing contingencies and a closing date that has to suit a lender.

An investor planning a rental may close sooner, especially when a rental permit or student home license is already in place. A direct cash purchase drops the financing step and takes the property as is, with an offer that accounts for repairs. Get price, closing date and the 3 percent tax split in writing before you commit.

sections.h2: What should you confirm before accepting an offer?
sections.html:
• Locate your deed. If it is missing, contact the Centre County Recorder of Deeds.
  • Request a payoff figure from your lender to see what remains after the mortgage clears.
  • Settle who pays the 3 percent transfer tax before you sign.
  • Confirm whether the house has a rental housing permit, student home license or short-term rental license, and disclose it.
  • Gather receipts for roof, furnace, drainage and plumbing work.
  • Check that property tax bills are current, since unpaid balances come out of your proceeds at closing.

At the closing table the title agent totals the payoff, any tax balance and the transfer tax, and the Recorder will not accept the new deed until that tax is paid. Buyers who pay cash skip the lender's appraisal, so a clean paper trail is usually the only thing that holds up a close.

faqs.q: Is State College's transfer tax really 3 percent?
faqs.a: Yes. Centre County's rate table puts the borough at 3.00 percent: 1.00 percent state, 1.5 percent local and 0.50 percent school district. Most other municipalities in the county total 2.00 percent. Buyers and sellers often divide it equally, but the contract decides.

faqs.q: Does a student home license go to the buyer?
faqs.a: It can. The borough lets an existing license pass to a new owner once a transfer application is approved and a $25 fee is paid. Email studenthomes@statecollegepa.us for the current application before you advertise the license as part of the sale.

faqs.q: Does a rented house need a rental permit to sell?
faqs.a: The permit is a condition of renting, so a rented house should hold a current Rental Housing Permit from Centre Region Code Administration. Check the permit status first, because a lapsed permit can worry a buyer.

faqs.q: Who handles trash and water in State College?
faqs.a: Borough public works collects trash and recycling, and the State College Borough Water Authority provides water. Sewer service comes from the University Area Joint Authority.

faqs.q: How can I obtain my State College deed?
faqs.a: Contact the Centre County Recorder of Deeds, which holds the recorded deed. The office will not accept a new deed for recording until the transfer taxes due have been paid.
